notes: FIRST REVIEW, recorded under the owner ruling R11-1 in the r11 closure mandate, which states the proposition verbatim and says it authorizes the claim: "An authoritative admission state accepted by the enforcement point is authenticated as issued by the configured admission authority, bound to the workload and admission generation/status, and current within the deployment's declared revocation-currentness budget. Redis write access without the admission signing authority can deny service but cannot mint or indefinitely replay an admission that restores service to a revoked or otherwise non-current workload." WHAT THE STATEMENT ADDS TO THAT WORDING: nothing about consequence. It generalises "Redis" to "the store" (the mechanism is not the claim, and the in-memory source is held to the same boundary), and it names the three coordinates that carry it — signature, subject comparison, currentness ceiling — each with the forgery the other two cannot see. WHAT IT DELIBERATELY DOES NOT CLAIM, all recorded in `scope`: it is V0, so tests plus a mutation self-test, NOT a proof, and the batteries passing is not evidence that a check is load-bearing; the observed publication-sequence floor is HARDENING and outside the claim, because a replica that has just started has no floor and a restart forgets one; Redis ACLs and compare-and-set appear as no premise at all, and no assumption registers the store as trusted — that framing is what this result removes; availability is not claimed, and an authority that fails to republish inside its own declared budget will see admission lapse, which is inside the claim rather than a violation of it. Registered as a SUBORDINATE of THM-0004 rather than a widening of it, as the ruling directs: THM-0004 keeps "given state X, does this call match X?" and this answers "why is X an authenticated, sufficiently current statement from the configured authority?".
